en: The Theravāda Vinaya Mahāvibhaṅga:
The Section on the Training Rules (Sekhiyakaṇḍa)
Ujjagghikavagga 20.
The Second Training Rule on Shaking the Head.
At that time, the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
Now at that time, the group-of-six monks sat in inhabited areas swaying their heads, letting their heads hang down... [etc. ...
"The training is to be observed: 'I shall not sit in an inhabited area swaying my head.
One must not sit in an inhabited area swaying one's head.
One should sit with the head held up.
Whoever, out of disrespect, sits in an inhabited area shaking his head or letting it hang down, commits an offense of wrong-doing (*dukkaṭa*).
There is no offense—
Unintentionally,
through lack of mindfulness,
or without knowing.
For one who is ill,
for one who has entered a residence,
and in times of distress.
"In the case of one who is insane,
or in the case of the first offender.
The tenth training rule is concluded.
The Second Chapter on Excessive Laughter.
